claims.text: The baseline MnNiSi-based alloy exhibits a first-order magnetostructural transition that produces a large magnetocaloric effect.
The baseline MnNiSi-based alloy suffers from brittleness.
The baseline MnNiSi-based alloy has poor fracture toughness.
Adding approximately 1–2 at.% Nb will improve the mechanical performance of MnNiSi-based magnetocaloric alloys.
Low-level Nb addition will refine the grain structure.
Low-level Nb addition will nucleate fine Nb-rich precipitates along grain boundaries.
Low-level Nb addition will nucleate fine Nb-rich precipitates within the matrix.
The proposed Nb-rich precipitates will be ductile.
The Nb-induced microstructure will impede crack propagation.
Adding 1–2 at.% Nb will not cause major alterations in the parent lattice.
Nb-induced grain refinement will improve mechanical robustness through grain-boundary strengthening.
Nb-rich precipitates will improve mechanical robustness through precipitation hardening.
At a concentration of 1–2 at.%, Nb will minimally perturb the magnetostructural phase transition.
The Nb-modified alloy will show at least a 20% improvement in tensile ductility relative to the Nb-free baseline.
The Nb-modified alloy will show at least a 20% improvement in fracture toughness relative to the Nb-free baseline.
The isothermal entropy change of the Nb-modified alloy will be reduced by less than 10% relative to the Nb-free baseline.
The beneficial balance of mechanical and magnetocaloric properties is limited to a narrow Nb concentration window of approximately 1–2 at.%.
Exceeding the proposed Nb concentration window may alter the magnetostructural transition or form unwanted phases that degrade magnetocaloric properties.
